## Upstream changes v11.4.3 -> v11.5.0

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — the notes describe Cloud-side features, UI/bugfixes and a swarm fix; the image configuration (user, entrypoint, command, ports, volumes, healthcheck, environment) is unchanged, and no companion-service version requirement is introduced.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none — no renamed, removed, or newly required variables in the notes, and the images' environment configuration is confirmed identical (`WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN`)

### Data and dependencies
- none. The notes mention no database, cache or search engine version requirement for this range. All companion images in the compose file (`traefik`, `dockerproxy`, `backups`) are unaffected since this is a Dozzle-only version bump.
- Two fixes are worth flagging as behavioural, not configuration, changes: **"Don't start or restart a swarm task container"** (`#5682`) affects anyone using Dozzle against a Swarm deployment, and **"Drop Podman's zero memory swappiness when recreating a container"** (`#5664`) affects hosts running under Podman — neither applies to this template's plain Docker/Traefik setup but are worth knowing if this host ever runs in either mode.

### Before applying
- Update the pin in `dozzle-traefik-letsencrypt-docker-compose.yml` from `v11.4.3@sha256:244f218c876d6ed766277e71a537f34bfb2c01829e1927737e3673a8327deeb8` to the corresponding `v11.5.0` tag and digest (or override via `DOZZLE_IMAGE_VERSION`/`DOZZLE_IMAGE_TAG` in `.env`).
- No data migration, no manual steps, no `.env.example` edits required.

### Notes read
- v11.5.0 (2026-11-19) — the release being moved to
- v11.4.3 (2026-11-13) — the baseline currently running, read only to exclude already-true requirements
- No UPGRADING/BREAKING_CHANGES/CHANGELOG section was supplied for this range; none to weigh against the release notes above.

## Upstream changes 19.5.6 -> 19.6.1

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no release notes could be read for this range, and the image configurations could not be compared either, so this upgrade cannot be verified from any source; treat it as unverified until checked by hand.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes — the notes source returned "no releases between 19.5.6 and 19.6.1 found under gitlabhq/gitlabhq (0 releases read), and no tag range compared." This is an absence of data, not a confirmation of safety.

### Variables
- none found — with no notes and no readable image config, no renamed, removed, or newly required variables can be identified. The compose file's current variables (`GITLAB_DB_PASSWORD`, `GITLAB_URL`, `GITLAB_HOSTNAME`, etc.) are unaffected as far as can be determined, but this is not verified against 19.6.1.

### Data and dependencies
- Already true at the current version (19.5.6), not a change introduced by this range: the compose file pins Postgres 17 and sets `max_locks_per_transaction=256`, `shared_buffers=256MB` on the comment basis of "GitLab's external-database guidance" — this is pre-existing configuration, not something this upgrade requires.
- Whether GitLab 19.6.1 raises its minimum supported PostgreSQL version, changes required Postgres extensions, or alters any other external dependency cannot be determined — the release notes were not available.

### Before applying
- Take a full GitLab backup (application data + `/etc/gitlab` config + the `gitlab-postgres` volume) before touching the running stack, per the project's own README backup procedure, since no migration-safety information is available from upstream notes.
- Manually check the following before upgrading, since the automated sources failed:
  - GitLab's own release posts / "What's new" pages for 19.6.0 and 19.6.1 on about.gitlab.com.
  - The GitLab `UPGRADING.md` / upgrade-path documentation (docs.gitlab.com) for any required intermediate versions — GitLab sometimes mandates stepping-stone releases.
  - The GitLab CHANGELOG in the `gitlabhq/gitlabhq` repo directly (tags `v19.6.0-ee` / `v19.6.1-ee`) in case the releases API path used here missed them.
  - Confirm whether 19.6.x changes the minimum PostgreSQL version (GitLab has a documented minimum; check it still allows Postgres 17, which this compose file pins).
  - Diff the image's default `gitlab.rb` / omnibus template between the two tags if available, since `GITLAB_OMNIBUS_CONFIG` here is a partial override and any new mandatory setting would otherwise go unnoticed.
- Do not treat the absence of notes as evidence of a safe upgrade; schedule this as an attended upgrade with rollback (volume snapshot) ready.

### Notes read
- None. The upstream source reported zero releases found between 19.5.6 and 19.6.1 under `gitlabhq/gitlabhq`, and no tag range could be compared. The registry image inspection also failed (404), so the "what the images differ in" comparison could not be used either.

## Upstream changes 19.5.6 -> 19.5.8

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — the upstream release notes for this range could not be found, so the upgrade's actual content is unverified; nothing here confirms it is safe, and nothing here confirms it is dangerous either.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes — because no notes were available to read. Do not read this as "no breaking changes exist"; it means the claim cannot be made either way.

### Variables
- none identified. The compose file's `x-images` pin (`GITLAB_IMAGE_VERSION:-19.5.6-ee.0`) would need to move to `19.5.8-ee.0` (or the matching `-ee.0` suffix GitLab ships for that patch) as part of applying this upgrade — that is a mechanical pin change, not a notes-derived variable change.

### Data and dependencies
- The compose file pins `postgres:17` and this is already true at 19.5.6 (baseline, not introduced by this range) — not a decision point for this verdict.
- Whether GitLab 19.5.8 raises or keeps its minimum PostgreSQL requirement is unknown without the release/upgrade notes. GitLab historically gates minor/patch releases on a minimum PostgreSQL version; if 19.5.8's notes specify a floor higher than 17, this compose file's Postgres pin would need to be checked against it before applying. This could not be confirmed here.

### Before applying
- Take a GitLab backup before upgrading, per the project's own documented procedure (`gitlab-backup.sh` referenced in this repo's README), since no migration notes are available to say whether 19.5.8 includes irreversible database migrations.
- Manually check the GitLab release/upgrade documentation for 19.5.7 and 19.5.8 (patch releases between 19.5.6 and 19.5.8) before proceeding — specifically:
  - the GitLab "Deprecations and removals" / upgrade notes for the 19.5.x patch series,
  - the required PostgreSQL version stated for 19.5.8,
  - whether any background migration must finish before upgrading further (GitLab enforces this between certain versions).
- Confirm the exact image tag/digest for `gitlab/gitlab-ee:19.5.8-ee.0` exists and update both the `x-images` default in the compose file and, if pinned, `GITLAB_IMAGE_VERSION` in `.env`.

### Notes read
- None. The upstream source reports: "no releases between 19.5.6 and 19.5.8 found under gitlabhq/gitlabhq (0 releases read), and no tag range compared." The registry image-diff also could not be read (404). This review is based solely on the compose file and `.env.example` as given; it does not substitute for reading GitLab's own release/upgrade notes by hand before applying.

## Upstream changes 8.9.1 -> 9.0.0

**Verdict:** DO NOT APPLY UNATTENDED — this release removes local login providers (Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress, Dolphin) and gates LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth behind a Premium license; any deployment using these methods without a Premium plan will have users locked out, including possibly all admins.

### Breaking changes
- **LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth become Premium-only.** From the version banner: *"LDAP, SAML, and Custom OAuth now require a premium plan... Community workspaces that use any of these must upgrade their plan or move users to a supported login method before updating, or those users won't be able to log in."* Confirmed in Major Changes: *"Makes LDAP and SAML authentication Premium features. **Breaking:** workspaces without a Premium plan that includes the `ldap-enterprise` or `saml-enterprise` module lose LDAP and SAML login on upgrade to 9.0.0."*
- **Several OAuth login providers removed outright**, not just gated: *"Removes the built-in Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress and Dolphin OAuth login providers."* Users of these keep their accounts but need another login method.
- **Webhook integration scripts no longer transpiled with Babel**, run in strict mode: *"Stopped transpiling webhook integration scripts with Babel. Scripts now run as-is inside `isolated-vm`... Scripts that relied on sloppy-mode behaviors... must be updated."* Custom webhook scripts can break silently.
- **157 Meteor/DDP methods removed**: *"External DDP/SDK clients that still invoke these by name will receive a `Method 'X' not found [404]` error."* Affects any custom integration or bot using the Realtime API directly rather than REST.
- **REST API error status codes changed**: 401 vs 403 semantics reshuffled, error bodies change shape (`errorType` now `error-forbidden`, no `status`/`message` on 401, etc.) across multiple PRs (#43138, #43214, #42741). Any script or integration parsing these codes/bodies needs review.
- **Custom scripts relying on Meteor client packages break**: *"The web client no longer ships Meteor's client packages... Code that runs in the page and relies on those packages stops working, in particular the custom scripts of `Custom_Script_On_Logout`, `Custom_Script_Logged_Out` and `Custom_Script_Logged_In`..."*
- **Anonymous write/login removed**: *"Removes the 'Allow Anonymous Write' setting... any existing users holding the `anonymous` role are deactivated and logged out."*
- **Atlassian Crowd integration removed**; affected users must switch authentication method.
- **WebDAV, Gravatar, legacy Matrix/federation, legacy GCM push removed** — see Variables and Data sections below.
- **`/ufs` legacy file-download endpoint removed.**
- **`query`/`fields` REST parameters removed**, along with the env var that re-enabled them (see Variables).

### Variables
- `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` — removed: *"Removes the deprecated `query` and `fields` REST API parameters, along with the `ALLOW_UNSAFE_QUERY_AND_FIELDS_API_PARAMS` environment variable that re-enabled them."* Not referenced by this compose/.env, but check custom deployments if anyone layered it in.
- `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` — default changes from `0` (unlimited) to `10000`: *"Changes the default value of the `MESSAGE_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH` environment variable from `0` (no limit) to `10000` characters."* Not set in the compose file or `.env.example`, so the host will pick up the new default silently; workspaces with `Message_MaxAllowedSize` above the default 5000 and messages routinely over 10,000 chars will see long messages stop rendering as markdown.
- `Push_UseLegacy`, `Push_gcm_project_number`, `Push_gcm_api_key` — removed (dead settings, no effect expected).
- `Accounts_OAuth_Use_Modern_Flow`, `Accounts_OAuth_Proxy_host`, `Accounts_OAuth_Proxy_services` — removed.
- `CROWD_*` settings — removed.
- `FEDERATION_*` / `Federation_Matrix_*` legacy settings — removed.
- `Use_RC_SDK` — removed, no effect expected.
- None of the above are referenced in this template's compose file or `.env.example`, so no edit is required there.

### Data and dependencies
- **MongoDB 8.0** is required by 9.0.0's own engine table (`MongoDB: 8.0`). The compose file already pins `mongo:8.0@sha256:...` and the baseline 8.9.1 release already required MongoDB 8.0 — this is not a new requirement introduced by this upgrade, just confirmation the existing pin still satisfies it.
- **Node 24.22.1 / Debian bookworm**: per the summary, *"The official Docker images move to Node.js 24.22.1 on Debian bookworm."* This was already true at 8.9.1 per the baseline notes (*"Bump the Node.js base image of the Docker images to 24.22.1... Debian image moves from bullseye to bookworm"*), so it is not a new change in this range.
- **Automatic data migrations on upgrade** (irreversible in the sense that rollback would leave the new shape behind):
  - `phone` user field migrated to `phones` array: *"the `phone` user field is replaced by the `phones` array... existing numbers are migrated automatically on upgrade."*
  - `freeSwitchExtension` renamed to `sipExtension`, migrated automatically.
  - Push token documents reshaped (flat `tokenValue`/`tokenType`, VoIP tokens split into their own document).
  - Unused MongoDB indexes dropped (listed under #41974).
  - Stale `Drafts` sidebar group migrated out of user preferences.
  - `anonymous`-role users deactivated and logged out; the role and its setting deleted.
  - CROWD_*, WebDAV, legacy federation/Matrix, legacy GCM push settings deleted from the database.
- **`Livechat_enabled` (Omnichannel) default changes to `false` for new workspaces only** — existing workspaces keep their current value, so this does not affect an already-running deployment being upgraded.
- No change to exposed ports, volumes, or container user/entrypoint — confirmed identical by the image comparison.

### Before applying
- **Before upgrading, confirm at least one administrator can log in with a local username and password.** Per the notes: *"Before you update: make sure at least one administrator can log in with a local username and password."* This is the single most important step — read https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/prepare-for-authentication-changes-in-9-0-0 first.
- Check whether this workspace holds a Premium license with `ldap-enterprise`, `saml-enterprise`, or `oauth-enterprise` modules. If it does not, and LDAP, SAML, or Custom OAuth are in use, either obtain the license or migrate affected users to local/Google/GitHub/GitLab/Apple/Nextcloud login **before** upgrading.
- Check whether any users signed in via Drupal, Facebook, GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn, Meteor, Twitter, WordPress, or Dolphin OAuth; they keep their accounts but need an alternate login method afterward.
- Review any custom webhook integration scripts for sloppy-mode JavaScript (implicit globals, `arguments.callee`, octal literals, duplicate parameters) — they will throw under strict mode.
- Review any external bots/integrations using Realtime API (DDP) method calls directly against the removed-methods list; migrate them to the listed REST equivalents.
- Review any external tooling that parses REST API error codes/bodies for the 401/403 and `errorType` reshuffle.
- Take a MongoDB backup before upgrading (the template's `backups` service already runs on a schedule — trigger or confirm a fresh backup exists immediately before the upgrade, given the automatic schema migrations and index drops).
- No compose file or `.env.example` edits are required for this upgrade.

### Notes read
- Release notes for 9.0.0 (RocketChat/Rocket.Chat), full Summary, Major Changes, Minor Changes and Patch Changes sections.
- Baseline notes for 8.9.1, used only to confirm which engine/Node/Debian requirements predate this upgrade.
